entries.notes: Focused regression passed. Windows post-build runtime dependency deployment now hashes source and destination before copying, so the editor-owned but byte-identical SDL2d.dll no longer turns a successful link into a failed build; a real urpg_tests relink completed through the new rule. Full clean-candidate build evidence remains pending because the implementation worktree is intentionally dirty.

Deliberately stale runtime rejection passed. The CMake/Ninja runtime-DLL rule now uses a Windows PowerShell 5.1/PowerShell 7 compatible SHA-256 helper, skips byte-identical locked DLLs, and still copies or fails truthfully when content differs. Configure and an actual urpg_tests link/post-build completed successfully. Clean qualification emission remains pending.

entries.notes: Creator journey, vertical slice, spatial, and supporting focused lanes pass. The prior editor-owned SDL2d.dll post-build false failure is resolved by hash-aware runtime dependency deployment. Strict PFU-I1 qualification still correctly rejects the dirty worktree; clean Debug/Release, package/install, and manual evidence remain open.
Scope ledger and admission rule are implemented; clean-commit evidence remains pending.
Strict gate correctly rejects four accepted open P0 defects; clean-commit evidence remains pending.
All 13 durable native editor documents have explicit owner, save, history, recovery, migration, reference, and gap status; clean-commit evidence remains pending.

Typed deterministic graph, canonical project-root rebuild, atomic incremental replacement, rebuild equivalence, inbound/outbound, and package-inclusion queries pass within the 68-assertion 7-case focused suite. Extractors cover maps/events/switches/variables/assets, dialogue, quests, menus, database records, gameplay recipes, MZ plugins, and native mods. Clean-commit evidence remains pending.

Revision admission, prepare/commit, rollback, idempotent replay, inverse revision guards, and composite undo/redo pass within the 40-assertion 5-case focused suite. Durable journaling and real domain-owner adapters remain in progress.

Named find-uses, outbound-reference, and package-inclusion explanations return stable document/local-object navigation and reference types; the Asset Library context action now uses the authoritative graph. The focused suite passes 68 assertions in 7 cases; broader golden-slice editor context integrations and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

Read-only rename/move/delete/replace/relink planning reports exact source navigation, blocked inbound uses, package impact, stable-ID updates, and inverse requests; 22 assertions pass in 3 cases. Typed owner application and save/reopen/playtest/undo round trips remain in progress.

One multi-owner intent exposes one stable label and one composite undo/redo boundary with stale-revision refusal; 40 assertions pass in 5 cases. Editor history wiring and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

Atomic prepared/committed journal records retain owner revisions and recovery snapshots; fault injection proves failed replacement preserves the last acknowledged state, and operation IDs enforce a single prepare/commit sequence. The focused suite passes 28 assertions in 3 cases. Coordinator wiring and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

Forward-only version discovery, full-chain copy preflight, dry run, atomic authoritative mutation, backup restore, idempotence, and failure rollback pass 30 assertions in 3 cases. Real document step registration, oldest-fixture corpus, disk backups, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

Read-only inspection distinguishes unchanged, dirty modified conflict, renamed, deleted, and malformed files and offers compare/reload/keep-local without mutation; 16 assertions pass in 3 cases. File-watcher/editor flow integration and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

The original playful-workshop token model covers semantic colors, typography, spacing, radius, borders, elevation, icons, motion, sound, focus, density, and scale for light/dark/high-contrast themes; contrast, gallery shape, 50%-300% scale, and reduced motion pass 77 assertions in 2 cases. Editor-wide adoption, snapshots, raw-constant audit, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

Persisted UI scale now applies globally to ImGui fonts and style metrics at startup, semantic light/dark/high-contrast tokens drive core style roles, and supported 50%-300% token bounds pass within the 77-assertion suite. Live scale rebuild, fixed-canvas conversion, route-by-scale snapshots/manual review, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

Blocker validation, private current-map overlays, selected-object launch metadata, disposable launch checkpoint, and explicit return-to-editor context pass 33 assertions in 2 cases. The clean qualification source now authors a real native event before playtest and compiles with generated build defines; current-candidate interactive qualification and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

A shared editor widget-state contract covers buttons, segmented controls, cards, fields, pickers, trees, tabs, tables, toasts, banners, progress jobs, empty states, diagnostics, confirmations, and command previews across normal/hover/focus/pressed/disabled/loading/error; semantic roles and safe action gating pass 518 assertions in 2 cases. Shared ImGui renderers, panel adoption, visual snapshots, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

Recent, pinned, missing-project recovery, guided certified-template creation, settings, create-and-playtest, and native browse-backed open/create/locate paths pass 95 assertions in 9 cases. The startup capability matrix names every required destination and assigns enabled routes only to working flows, with explicit unavailable reasons for project import, pre-open health, and examples. First-class import, recovery-snapshot, project-health, and example startup routes plus first-user visual qualification and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

The supported Windows native folder picker is shared by asset import and startup create/open/missing-project locate flows, exposes truthful availability, retains typed path entry as the embedded fallback, and models cancellation as a safe empty optional; the focused picker suite passes 14 assertions in 1 case. macOS qualification, Linux fallback review, interactive cancellation evidence, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

The primary Map route exposes the seven required project navigator, context toolbar, central canvas, inspector, status/jobs, diagnostics, and playtest-control regions. Pane sizing and visibility persist through local settings; non-finite corruption and an explicit Reset Workspace Layout action restore defaults without changing project/map context. The focused suite passes 127 assertions in 7 cases and the editor application object compiles. Cross-route region adoption, visual layout qualification, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

A deterministic editor command catalog makes create project, open map, create event, save, current-map playtest, project health, and export validation searchable by labels, IDs, categories, keywords, help, and requirements. All golden-loop entries expose shortcuts, requirements, contextual help, enablement, deterministic ranking, shortcut discovery, and bounded MRU behavior; 53 assertions pass in 2 cases. Shell palette rendering, reference-index global object search, command dispatch adapters, shortcut/manual qualification, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

The 15-family shared widget matrix now assigns unique focus order, keyboard semantics, controller semantics, accessible names, non-pointer alternatives, visible focus, and loading/error/disabled announcements across all required states. The automated accessibility audit rejects missing names, missing semantics, missing alternatives, and duplicate focus positions; 839 assertions pass in 3 cases. Shared ImGui renderer adoption plus manual keyboard, controller, and screen-reader review on supported operating systems and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

The non-modal Creator Checklist derives progress from durable project artifacts, recognizes explicit sample projects, identifies the next incomplete step, and supplies contextual route/action/help coaching for hero art, map editing, player start, NPC event, dialogue, playtest, save, and validation. Dismissal, completion, restoration, and replay count persist atomically per project; replay reopens coaching without changing project content. The focused suites pass 68 assertions in 4 cases. Wizard sample-project selection, route-focus dispatch, unassisted new-user session observation, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

A validated editor error-card contract requires a plain summary, affected object, consequence, suggested fix, Go To action, Retry action, copy-details payload, and redacted support export. Recursive redaction removes credential-bearing fields and filesystem paths; raw std:: diagnostics and dead-end cards are rejected. Startup project-open failures now emit this actionable card while retaining compatibility text. The focused error and startup suites pass 113 assertions in 11 cases. Error-corpus conversion/audit across all panels, shared visual renderer adoption, interactive action dispatch, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

One cooperative durable job contract now covers scan, import, hash, thumbnail, transform, audio-analysis, and package stages with monotonic stage/overall progress, bounded incremental reporting, cancellation, resume, failure retry, ordered logs, attempts, atomic checkpoints, and interrupted-running recovery into an explicit paused state. Cancellation and restart are exercised at every stage, and checkpoint/recovery/retry behavior passes 108 assertions in 2 cases. Real scan/import/thumbnail/audio/package worker adapters, editor jobs UI, large-fixture responsiveness budgets, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

The catalog now combines existing collections, favorites, rich quick/facet filters, provenance, license, usage references, and package readiness with persisted named searches and two-to-four-asset comparison rows. Browser/action rows expose explicit usage_count, provenance, and package_status fields. Curation/settings persistence passes 60 assertions in 2 cases. The deterministic 100,000-row fixture passes 8 assertions; this run recorded fixture generation 4868 ms, catalog load 9 ms, and a 50,000-match filtered page query 2689 ms. Visual comparison UI adoption, interactive responsiveness capture, broader query-index optimization, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

One asset lifecycle orchestration service now normalizes relink, detach, replace, deduplicate, rename, move, and delete through ProjectReferenceIndex impact previews, ProjectReferenceChangePlan package/reference effects, and ProjectOperationCoordinator typed-owner execution. Deduplication requires equal non-empty hashes; referenced detach/delete are refused; successful multi-owner intent exposes one stable label and undo/redo boundary. The focused suite passes 42 assertions in 2 cases. Concrete map/dialogue/menu/database owner adapters, attachment file detach/move transactions, save/reopen/playtest/package round trips, editor impact UI, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

The non-destructive revision pipeline covers crop/scale, ordered manual palettes, deterministic palette extraction, fixed-point dithering, atlas metadata, loose-spritesheet slicing metadata, tileset grid rules, and retained promoted source payloads. Every manifest binds the immutable source revision and transformation parameters into a deterministic derived revision; identical work reuses the revision and pixel/metadata outputs are asserted. The transform and spritesheet suites pass 155 assertions in 4 cases. Broader golden image corpus, visual editor comparison/revert UX, real package round trip, and clean-commit evidence remain pending. Windows fixture streams were also closed explicitly so teardown no longer falsely fails on locked manifests.

Existing waveform/spectrogram inspection and deterministic trim/fade/gain/loop revisions are now complemented by one actionable PCM QA analyzer for clipping, effective silence, high average level, invalid/risky loop seams, missing rights, voice locale/take, caption, and muted-alternative metadata. The curated clipping/silence/bad-loop/missing-caption/muted-alternative corpus passes 16 assertions in 2 cases; governed voice metadata passes 17 assertions in 1 case, and the broader transform suite passes 143 assertions. True integrated LUFS calibration, codec-wide corpus, shared editor QA renderer, caption editing integration, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

One shared use-here compatibility contract now covers map tile, map prop, map event sprite, battle asset, menu image, portrait, animation, and audio destinations. Each compatible destination exposes picker, drag/drop, keyboard, and owner-undo paths; raw/unattached assets, incompatible targets, media-kind mismatches, and owners without undo are refused with explicit codes and reasons. Asset Library picker metadata advertises the eight governed destination selectors, and the focused suite passes 70 assertions in 2 cases. Concrete destination-owner mutation adapters, end-to-end undo/save/playtest/package round trips, manual UI input verification, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

Archive listing refuses traversal, absolute/device paths, encrypted entries, symbolic links, unsupported formats, excessive entry counts, aggregate expansion, per-entry expansion, and dangerous compression ratios before extraction. A deterministic portable-source custody audit resolves project-relative sources, detects missing project/external files, and enforces reject, allow-nonportable, or require-project-copy policy with package gating for required sources. The full focused suite passes 31 assertions in 5 cases; adversarial and custody subsets pass 6 and 13 assertions respectively. Release-validator/import-session wiring, real RAR/7z adversarial fixtures, interactive remediation UI, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

A deterministic third-party asset notices/BOM generator now derives package rows from governed AssetRecord provenance and authored rights metadata, sorts them independently of input order, and emits stable JSON plus reviewed human-readable notice text. Configurable policy fails packaging closed for unresolved license, source, rights-review, or export-eligibility metadata while excluding non-runtime source-only records by default. The focused suite passes 14 assertions in 2 cases. Export-packager file emission, reviewer approval/signoff UI, package-content round trip, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

MapAuthoringWorkspace now exposes one canonical map route for project, object, asset, diagnostic, and playtest entry sources. Routing preserves project root, active map identity, object/event/part identity, viewport focus, and maps each source to the correct existing authoring mode without converting child documents; missing map identity is refused without changing context. Route-equivalence passes 53 assertions in 1 case and the full Map-authoring suite passes 180 assertions in 8 cases. Application-shell dispatch replacement, duplicate-route removal audit, manual navigation recording, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

The native Perspective 2D owner now accepts atomic erase as well as upsert tile edits. A shared batch-edit layer supplies point, box, and lasso selection plus cut, paste, duplicate, move, fill, line, rectangle, replace, and stamp previews that resolve to one reviewed owner command; existing layer multi-select/visibility/lock/duplicate/delete remains intact. The focused suite passes 25 assertions in 2 cases, including 13 round-trip assertions proving destructive move, undo/redo, save, and reopen. Prop/event multi-selection and batch property editing, interactive clipboard/gesture adapters, runtime projection round trip, larger-map performance, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

Smart-prefab placement now uses version-independent stable operation instance IDs and records a stable group ID. The lifecycle owner previews affected instances and deterministic dependency closure, updates matched operations, adds/removes version operations, preserves explicit instance property overrides, and supports content-preserving detach; update and detach both execute through one native bulk-history boundary. The focused suite passes 21 assertions in 1 case including update, override preservation, add, undo/redo, detach, and detach undo. Placement/editor update UI, serialized save/reopen and runtime/package closure round trips, multi-group conflict handling, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

Perspective 2D tile metadata already supports autotile families, directional passability, collision, terrain tags, region IDs, priority, and star passability. A new workspace quality report now audits painted cells for missing governed definitions/material payloads, missing autotile family, adjacent seam passability mismatch, collision/passability conflict, blocked navigation start, and unreachable entrance goals; every diagnostic carries exact layer, tileset, tile, and cell identity. The focused adversarial map passes 18 assertions in 1 case. Interactive collision/navigation overlays, passability/terrain/region paint gestures, broader seam and entrance corpus, runtime/package round trip, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

A durable project world graph now owns named maps, entrances, exits, checkpoints, spawn points, conditional routes, object-linked invalid-reference diagnostics, orphan-map detection, deterministic JSON persistence, and transfer resolution to authored entrance coordinates. The focused suite passes 25 assertions in 2 cases; its golden slice authors and simulates a condition-gated town-to-forest transfer and unconditional return loop, then proves checkpoints/spawns and graph identity survive round trip. Map workspace graph editor, event-command synchronization, live runtime scene transfer/playtest, project save-file placement, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

PlaytestSessionController now supports coordinate-based play-from-here, a structured session-local teleport_here command channel, normal return-to-editor selection, and diagnostic-to-cell return context. Map, cell spawn, selected object, and checkpoint identity remain authoritative across launch, teleport, diagnostic focus, and return; unsafe map/coordinate requests remain refused. The spatial bridge passes 15 assertions in 1 case and the complete controller suite passes 48 assertions in 3 cases. Runtime-side command consumption, live scene teleport acknowledgement, Map workspace button adapters, manual cross-process focus recording, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

ProjectWorldGraph now produces a deterministic minimap/world preview with map nodes, route edges, condition keys, stable positions, and orphan state. Entrance/exit/checkpoint/spawn marker change previews identify the exact object and enumerate every affected route with source/target role and counterpart map; a reviewed entrance rename rewrites all affected route references before graph validation. The impact slice passes 19 assertions in 1 case and the full graph suite passes 44 assertions in 3 cases. Visual Map panel rendering/interaction, reviewed deletion application, event-command synchronization, save/package round trip, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

A production spatial budget evaluator now checks cells, layers, events, undo bytes, and snapshot latency and responds with measured diagnostics plus bounded degradation of event labels, live navigation preview, and snapshot frequency. The real stress fixture creates 48 layers, paints 4,096 cells, authors 512 events, maintains owner history, and serializes the native document; this run produced a 983,037-byte snapshot in 173 ms. The suite passes 60 assertions in 1 case, and an overload corpus triggers all five warnings with the intended degradation policy. Larger 256k-cell hardware matrix, repeated undo-memory measurement, interactive frame pacing capture, release budget signoff, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

The native EventCommandKind schema now covers conditions/branches, loops/breaks, waits/timers, parallel lanes, switch/variable/self-switch state, movement routes, camera, animation, audio, common events, transfer, battle, shop, item/gold, fade, and controlled script/extension calls. One authoritative 26-row capability matrix binds each command to authoring UI, serialization key, runtime effect, diagnostics, undo support, and controlled-call policy; a UI-neutral executor proves state, branch/loop, timing, action, and allowlist effects. The matrix/executor suite passes 199 assertions in 2 cases and existing EventDocument serialization/validation remains green at 24 assertions in 6 cases. Nested native compiler/scene adapters, real editor insertion widgets and history, full runtime-effect integrations, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

A structured native event sequence model now provides command search, favorite/recent ranking, validated templates, copy/paste with unique IDs, transactional reorder, atomic multi-edit, collapse/indent projection, and keyboard move/copy/paste/delete/collapse operations. Every mutation validates condition/else/end and loop/end nesting and restores the prior sequence on corruption. The focused suite passes 25 assertions in 2 cases, including a 1,004-command nested event copied to 2,008 commands, invalid reorder/delete rollback, template insertion, search/favorites, and keyboard paths. Event graph/panel rendering integration, persisted user favorites/recent, real undo stack, controller accessibility/manual navigation, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

A shared EventReferencePickerCatalog now covers maps, map entries, events, actors, items, skills, switches, variables, common events, audio, animations, quests, and dialogue. Search is human-label/detail driven and deterministic; unavailable/stale options fail explicitly, while successful binding stores stable ID, label, owner, and type in the native command payload instead of requiring raw numeric entry. The focused suite passes 91 assertions in 2 cases across all 13 domains and typed transfer/item/state/common-event/audio/animation mappings. Project reference-index population adapters, shared visual picker widgets, find-uses navigation, manual golden-loop proof, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

A native EventDocument static analyzer now combines existing reference validation with source-linked checks for commands after terminal effects, missing references, tight loops, infinite loops, unsafe parallel writes, transfer dead ends, missing localization IDs, voiced messages without captions, and autorun softlock risk. Findings carry severity, event/page/command identity, explanation, and actionable remediation. The curated bad/clean corpus passes 27 assertions in 2 cases, proving every requested hazard family and a finding-free localized two-way transfer. Diagnostics-panel integration, review/suppression workflow, larger false-positive calibration corpus, live runtime correlation, and clean-commit evidence remain pending.

Dialogue choices and quest nodes now support deterministic reorder, while quest graphs expose visual-authoring mutations for node create/remove, connect/disconnect, and canvas placement. A unified branching-quest document cross-validates dialogue-choice quest conditions, migrates legacy v1/editor-shaped data, collects deterministic voice/caption/localization/quest package closure, drives dialogue choices into quest runtime progress, and preserves runtime state through save/load. The focused voiced branching quest passes 26 assertions in 2 cases; dialogue and quest regressions pass 88 assertions in 6 cases and 36 assertions in 4 cases. The monolithic executable linked successfully, then the known running-editor SDL2d.dll post-build copy failed with permission denied. Concrete ImGui graph gestures, undo/history integration for these mutations, real project-file/package writer integration, manual visual/accessibility proof, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

A project-level EventTemplateLibrary now supports reusable common-event and narrative templates with typed string/integer/boolean/reference parameters, defaults, deterministic substitution, stable instances, per-command overrides, canonical CommonEventDefinition generation, persistence, dependency-backed find-uses, update/delete impact previews, versioned updates, safe deletion refusal, and replacement. Replacement preflights every instance and override before mutation; incompatible replacements fail atomically, while compatible updates and replacements preserve instance bindings, overrides, caller IDs, save-field metadata, payloads, and compatibility fallbacks. The focused suite passes 38 assertions in 2 cases; EventDocument and dependency-graph regressions pass 24 assertions in 6 cases and 6 assertions in 1 case. The test executable linked successfully before the known running-editor SDL2d.dll post-build copy denial. Visual library/picker UI, undo/history transaction wiring, project-file ownership, cross-document replacement UI, manual usability proof, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

EventDebugger now executes nested common events correctly through the authoritative native command executor and emits a bounded 4,096-entry runtime trace. Each entry identifies the current command and editor source route, event/page/command/index, stack depth, main or parallel lane, branch outcome, wait duration, result code, and before/after switch or variable mutations. Snapshots expose the next command/source, full stack, watched variables, branch depth, wait state, parallel lanes, and trace; any retained trace sequence resolves back to its exact event or common-event editor source. A failing ritual/quest corpus passes 19 assertions in 1 case across variable mutation, false branch, wait, parallel lane, nested common-event switch mutation, stack depth, and source navigation; existing debugger and native matrix suites pass 5 assertions in 1 case and 199 assertions in 2 cases. The executable linked before the known editor-owned SDL2d.dll copy denial. Live playtest transport, trace panel rendering/filtering, pause/resume timing semantics, parallel-lane scheduling visualization, source-opening UI, manual workflow proof, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

MZ event-command compatibility is now reported as a separate 13-row matrix with explicit opcodes, import strategies, and execution strategies instead of being folded into the native event-command authority. Supported commands translate to native commands; unsupported commands retain their raw structured payload losslessly and execute through explicit controlled or diagnostic fallback behavior for script, plugin, movie, and unknown opcodes. Unknown opcodes default to a preserved diagnostic no-op, and the coverage report explicitly separates compatibility coverage from the independent native command matrix. The focused compatibility suite passes 39 assertions in 3 cases; native command-matrix and EventDocument regressions pass 199 assertions in 2 cases and 24 assertions in 6 cases. The executable linked before the known editor-owned SDL2d.dll post-build copy denial. Broader MZ project-corpus/runtime-parity proof, plugin-specific behavior, manual workbench proof, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

A reusable editor-side ProjectDatabaseTableModel now exposes virtualized projections for actors, classes, skills, items, equipment, enemies, encounters, states, quests, vendors, recipes, switches, and variables without replacing their domain persistence authorities. Every table supports stable-id validation, deterministic case-insensitive search and field sorting, bounded visible windows, stable selection, and revisioned field edits that cannot mutate identity. Normalized search documents and sort keys are cached outside comparator loops for project-scale responsiveness. The existing native RpgDatabase actor/item authorities project into the table model, and the DatabasePanel reports all 13 views. A 50,000-row fixture plus all table kinds pass 72 assertions in 4 cases; the existing panel regression and broader database suite pass 5 assertions in 1 case and 88 assertions in 9 cases. The single-target urpg_tests build completed successfully; Ninja reported recovery from a premature build-log EOF but produced the source-matching executable. Concrete ImGui table/clipper rendering, adapters for the remaining fragmented domain authorities, manual latency captures, visible editing workflows, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

DatabaseBatchEditService now preflights fill, numeric formula, linear curve, stable-ID duplication, and structured import operations against a copied table projection, reporting every missing or invalid target before any mutation. Valid plans carry before/after snapshots, changed-row counts, the owning table kind, and a generation guard; apply is atomic, stale plans are rejected, and undo/redo refuse intervening edits. Export/import preserves row identity, names, summaries, typed field strings, and revisions, while duplicate/import validation rejects missing or repeated stable IDs. Focused batch coverage passes 40 assertions in 4 cases; PCQ-450 virtual-table regressions pass 72 assertions in 4 cases and the combined database tag passes 128 assertions in 13 cases. The source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully; Ninja recovered from its existing premature build-log EOF warning. Concrete multi-select/table UI, richer expression parsing and curve visualization, domain-level command/history adapters, CSV interchange, manual workflow proof, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

DatabaseReferenceWorkspace now maps all 13 golden-slice record tables onto the shared ProjectReferenceIndex and ProjectReferenceChangePlan authorities. It provides stable-ID/name picker options, bounded search, find-uses with document/local source identity, deterministic orphan detection, package-aware delete impact, and same-kind replacement preview with inverse details. Indexed inbound uses block deletion; unreferenced records preview as safe; replacements require both source and replacement records and produce no dangling target in the planned edge set. The adapter remains read-only so typed domain owners and ProjectOperationCoordinator retain mutation/undo authority. Focused database-reference coverage passes 75 assertions in 3 cases; reference-index and reference-change regressions pass 68 assertions in 7 cases and 22 assertions in 3 cases; the combined database tag passes 203 assertions in 16 cases. The source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Concrete picker/find-uses/impact UI, typed-owner apply adapters for every domain, cross-document commit tests, manual workflow proof, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

The existing EconomySimulator now supports versioned scenarios, seeded multi-iteration strategy/persona batches, configurable purchase behavior and reward multipliers, XP level curves, starting-gold sensitivity, reward-cadence budgets, required-purchase deadlock detection, and dominant-strategy comparison. Reports preserve scenario ID/version, seed, iteration count, explicit assumptions, per-strategy average gold/XP/level/deadlocks, sensitivity deltas, severity, exact step/parameter identity, and source-navigation routes. A nonlinear affordability fixture proves that sensitivity captures threshold effects rather than merely echoing the input delta. Focused scenario coverage passes 18 assertions in 2 cases; the legacy economy simulator and editor balance-panel regressions pass 4 assertions in 1 case and 5 assertions in 1 case. The source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Broader scenario libraries, percentile distributions, battle/vendor/crafting parameter adapters, simulation/history UI, calibrated grind heuristics, export reports, manual balance review, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

EconomyRevisionHistory now records immutable committed scenario snapshots with stable revision IDs, source revisions, deterministic content hashes, and their reproducible simulation reports. Recursive comparison covers scenario parameters and derived outcomes with JSON paths and numeric deltas. Deterministic review export embeds both hashed revisions, assumptions, strategies, sensitivities, findings, and the complete difference set without timestamps or ambient state. Restore is exposed only as a ProjectOperationParticipant, so the authoritative scenario changes through the existing ProjectOperationCoordinator with source-revision validation, rollback, labeled undo, and redo rather than through a second mutable balance store. Focused history coverage passes 41 assertions in 3 cases; project-operation coordinator and combined economy regressions pass 40 assertions in 5 cases and 63 assertions in 6 cases. The source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Concrete comparison/history UI, project-file persistence for committed review snapshots, report-file writing and redaction, manual review proof, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

DatabaseVerticalSliceIntegration now exercises one selected actor and stable record set through encounter/battle reward selection, inventory, equipment-tag validation, crafting output, vendor stock, quest completion, localization resolution, fresh-save rehydration, typed compat-save migration, and semantic package closure. The closure identifies every actor, item, enemy, encounter, quest, vendor, recipe, and localization key actually exercised. Save migration now recognizes a validated databaseState payload, maps it to native database_state without fallback, and preserves malformed state losslessly with an actionable diagnostic. A deliberately broken cross-domain fixture fails actor/item/equipment/battle/vendor/quest/localization/save checks before packaging. Focused vertical-slice and malformed-migration coverage pass 33 assertions in 2 cases and 4 assertions in 1 case; save-migration and combined database regressions pass 53 assertions in 6 cases and 236 assertions in 18 cases. The source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Full BattleScene combat execution, real package-file writer consumption of the semantic closure, migrated installed-package playthrough, concrete editor integration, manual proof, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

PlaytestHotReloadCoordinator now defines a bounded nine-class product matrix for maps, dialogue, quests, database, localization, audio, scripts, plugins, and renderer resources, then intersects it with runtime-advertised capabilities. Requests require stable safe IDs, non-empty payloads capped at 4 MiB, valid JSON for structured resources, optimistic source revisions, and an explicit preserve/reset-affected/reset-all policy. Preserve is allowed only where both sides support it. Hot-reloadable, restart-required, and rejected outcomes are explicit. A failed partial apply must roll back before restart fallback; rollback failure leaves revision unchanged and forbids unsafe restart. Focused capability/validation/apply/restart/recovery coverage passes 39 assertions in 5 cases; existing playtest session/overlay/return regressions pass 48 assertions in 3 cases. The warning-clean source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Live runtime transport/session-manifest wiring, concrete document-owner validators, visible reload controls/status, process-level restart verification, manual creator-loop proof, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

PlaytestRuntimeStateInspector now exposes typed switch, variable, self-switch, entity scalar-field, quest/objective, and inventory views with bounded watches. Safe temporary edits require unique mutation IDs, existing addresses, correct types, constrained numeric ranges, supported quest states, and scalar entity values. Every mutation retains before/after values and is explicitly marked temporary=true and packaged=false. The package projection remains immutable, disposable overlay export separates debug and package state, and reset restores an explicit named checkpoint while clearing the mutation ledger. Multiple bounded runtime checkpoints are supported without replacing the initial package authority. Focused inspector coverage passes 71 assertions in 4 cases; hot-reload and existing event-debugger regressions pass 39 assertions in 5 cases and 5 assertions in 1 case. The source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Live runtime snapshot/edit transport, visible inspector/watch UI and mutation styling, runtime acknowledgement, package-audit integration, manual debugging proof, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

EventDebugger now supports stable typed breakpoint records, variable/switch/self-switch conditions, enable/remove lifecycle, explicit manual pause and continue, single-command stepping, and deterministic frame advance only while paused on a native wait. Breakpoint hit counts, active breakpoint identity, runtime frame, current command source, full common-event call stack, and bounded before/after trace remain available in one snapshot. Legacy addBreakpoint and resume behavior are retained. Focused PCQ-503 coverage passes 42 assertions in 3 cases; PCQ-406 runtime trace and legacy debugger regressions pass 19 assertions in 1 case and 5 assertions in 1 case. The warning-clean source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Live runtime/editor transport, concrete breakpoint/source-focus UI, replay-clock integration beyond native waits, manual failing-event proof, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

ScenarioReplayCapture now records bounded typed semantic inputs with deterministic state hashes, seed, exact project revision, runtime version, sorted labeled checkpoints, redacted checkpoint previews, and an explicit redaction-field ledger. ReplayArtifact JSON remains backward compatible with legacy inputs while round-tripping the new capture fields. ScenarioReplayRunner gates execution on project/runtime identity, supports the same semantic executor in headless and interactive modes, and clearly reports missing executors, unsupported inputs, environment mismatch, or the first divergent tick with expected and actual hashes. Focused PCQ-504 coverage passes 40 assertions in 3 cases; legacy replay/gallery/golden regressions pass 38 assertions in 8 cases. The warning-clean source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Live runtime semantic-input capture/execution adapters, file persistence and signing, visible replay workflow, broader redaction corpus, manual reported-failure replay proof, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

PerformanceCapture now accepts bounded monotonic frame samples spanning total frame time, render, script/event, asset streaming, audio, and memory. Its overlay reports latest/average/maximum frame time, current subsystem timings and memory, plus the most recent retained spike. Threshold crossings are linked deterministically to frame index, timestamp, dominant subsystem, and dominant time; the stable local JSON report contains the same retained frames and spike attribution. Invalid ordering, zero-time samples, duplicate capture starts, and inactive recording are rejected. Focused PCQ-505 coverage passes 39 assertions in 3 cases; legacy PerfProfiler regressions pass 25 assertions in 7 cases. The warning-clean source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Runtime instrumentation wiring, concrete overlay/capture UI, GPU/allocator platform adapters, capture-file writing, manual visible-hitch proof, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

ProjectRecoveryCoordinator now provides one deterministic fault matrix for 13 canonical primary document types plus asset jobs, external-change conflicts, corrupted layout/settings, failed migrations, and failed packages. Every action identifies its owner, disposition, safe next action, automation boundary, user-choice requirement, and project-data preservation guarantee. Document recovery offers only private copies, conflicts require explicit resolution, asset jobs resume only from validated checkpoints, layouts may reset to safe defaults, migrations roll back only with a backup, and package failures preserve sources while discarding partial output. Missing classes, missing primary documents, duplicate IDs, and invalid rows make coverage incomplete. Focused fault-injection coverage passes 70 assertions in 3 cases. The warning-clean source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Concrete adapters that invoke each existing subsystem owner, visible recovery workflow, corrupted-settings quarantine persistence, process-level package cleanup, human walkthrough evidence, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

RedactedSupportBundleBuilder now assembles structured logs, diagnostics, versions, platform capabilities, project manifest hashes, optional replay, and explicitly opted-in selected project data. A mandatory preview lists included/excluded sections and every redaction before any write. Secret/credential keys, PII keys, filesystem-path keys, suspicious free-text credentials, embedded Windows paths, Unix/UNC paths, and email-like text are conservatively redacted; a corpus proves the source values do not survive serialization. Declined approval writes nothing. Approved output is published locally through a temporary file and rename, declares upload_performed=false, and exposes no network/upload API. Focused PCQ-507 coverage passes 30 assertions in 3 cases. The warning-clean source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Integration with live log/diagnostic/version/platform/manifest/replay providers, concrete preview UI, broader multilingual/encoded PII corpus, archive packaging, manual review evidence, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

RuntimePresentationBible now extends the existing URPG design-token authority with an original playful-workshop visual motif, six URPG-namespaced sound motifs, a four-tier bounded feedback hierarchy, particle limits and motifs, interruptible camera limits, and default/large-text/high-contrast/reduced-motion accessibility variants. Validation rejects foreign identities, missing sound roles, invalid or misordered feedback, unbounded particles/camera, inaccessible variants, and invalid token projections. A deterministic runtime component-showcase snapshot covers seven primary component families and their important states under every variant; reduced motion removes camera shake, zeros motion-token durations, and caps particle density. The candidate intent document is docs/product/runtime_presentation_bible.md and explicitly remains unapproved. Focused PCQ-600 coverage passes 45 assertions in 3 cases; existing design-token regressions pass 77 assertions in 2 cases. The warning-clean source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Design approval, concrete rendered component showcase, asset/audio motif review, runtime-owner adoption, screenshots/video, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

RuntimeShellFlow now provides one bounded state machine across startup/title/profile/save/settings/gameplay/pause/quit/error/exit while delegating actual new-game, load, save, settings, and process-exit operations to existing owners. It validates and stably orders profiles/saves, keeps invalid rows visible with actionable disabled reasons, restores focus after delegated settings, requires quit confirmation, and records every transition with sequence, source, destination, reason, <=250 ms duration, and immediate acknowledgement. Keyboard and generic-controller glyphs use URPG semantic asset IDs and update with the active device. A controller-only fixture completes startup, new-game profile selection, pause, save, settings return, and confirmed quit; another loads a valid save and rejects a corrupt one. Focused PCQ-601 coverage passes 62 assertions in 3 cases; runtime title and options regressions pass 99 assertions in 11 cases and 32 assertions in 2 cases; PCQ-600 presentation regressions pass 45 assertions in 3 cases. The warning-clean source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Concrete EngineShell/SceneManager wiring, rendered profile/save/pause/quit surfaces, actual connected-controller glyph-family detection, process-level save/load journey, capture/manual controller evidence, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

ExplorationFeedbackDirector now provides a bounded, prioritized sensory cue authority for interaction prompts and acknowledgement, pickups, rewards, doors, transfers, quest updates, dialogue cadence, and screen transitions. Every cue carries original URPG icon, sound, particle, camera, hierarchy, duration, and non-color metadata; higher-priority cues preempt without loss, duplicate requests are rejected, and active plus queued work is capped at 32. Audio-off and reduced-motion settings remove sound, particles, and camera cues as applicable, while dialogue speed remains bounded. MapScene advances and renders the active cue, emits unique interaction/dialogue/transfer requests, uses resolved localized dialogue text, and exposes a typed producer API for pickup/reward/quest owners. The legacy default-map TileData initializer was corrected to retain visible tiles after the existing hasVisual field addition. Focused exploration coverage passes 76 assertions in 2 cases; direct MapScene integration passes 4 assertions in 1 case; broader scene/map regressions pass 260 assertions in 37 cases; PCQ-600 presentation regressions pass 45 assertions in 3 cases. The source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Concrete pickup/reward/quest producer wiring, contextual sound playback consumption, rendered icon-asset resolution, frame-by-frame capture, sensory review, screenshots/video, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

entries.notes: BattleFeedbackDirector now provides a bounded prioritized vocabulary for command selection, targeting, turn state, anticipation, impact, damage, healing, status, victory, defeat, and results. Every cue has an original URPG icon and non-color shape, explicit hierarchy, bounded duration and hit stop, and declares that it never blocks control. Audio-off removes sounds; reduced motion removes particles, camera cues, and hit stop; monochrome and color-filter settings retain shape/text identity. Fast-forward shortens skippable cues and caps hit stop, while skip collapses only skippable cues and preserves full victory, defeat, and result readability. Active plus queued work is capped at 48 and higher-priority cues preempt without loss. BattleScene advances the director and emits unique phase, command, target, anticipation, impact, damage/heal, victory/defeat, and reward-result feedback while retaining the existing EffectCue authority. Focused accessibility and skip coverage passes 124 assertions in 2 cases; direct BattleScene integration passes 3 assertions in 1 case; existing effect-cue, native BattleScene, battle-core, and presentation-bible regressions pass 61 assertions in 6 cases, 137 assertions in 14 cases, 113 assertions in 11 cases, and 45 assertions in 3 cases. The source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Concrete sound/VFX/camera consumers, named status-change publication, result-screen rendering, color-filter renderer validation, representative encounter capture/manual sensory review, final battleback/assets, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

entries.notes: RuntimeFeedbackStack now defines one shared bounded authority for focus, confirm, cancel, error, and custom feedback with stable IDs, explicit ambient/secondary/primary/critical priorities, immediate acknowledgement, non-blocking control semantics, preemption without loss, duplicate rejection, and an active-plus-queued cap of 32. RuntimeFeedbackSettings centrally governs audio, optional haptics, particles, screen shake, hit stop, reduced motion, and intensity; treatment is clamped to the presentation bible's shake, hit-stop, duration, and hierarchy limits. Reduced motion replaces focus animation with an instant cue and clears particles, camera, shake, and hit stop. RuntimeShellFlow publishes its real startup, focus movement, command, cancel, save, pause, settings-return, and error paths through the stack. ExplorationFeedbackDirector and BattleFeedbackDirector use the same constraint function, and BattleScene's legacy shake timer now respects shake and reduced-motion settings. Focused PCQ-604 coverage passes 113 assertions in 4 cases; runtime shell, exploration, battle feedback, MapScene, BattleScene, and presentation-bible regressions pass 62 assertions in 3 cases, 76 assertions in 2 cases, 124 assertions in 2 cases, 260 assertions in 37 cases, 137 assertions in 14 cases, and 45 assertions in 3 cases. The source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully with the existing Ninja build-log recovery warning. Concrete AudioCore, controller-haptics, particle, camera, renderer-focus, and hit-stop consumers; persistent settings binding; hardware verification; screenshots/video; clean-commit evidence; and release signoff remain pending.

ReleaseSliceAssetAudit now defines the strict final-slice authority separately from the existing bounded-starter gate. It requires unique stable IDs and case-insensitively unique package paths; concrete bundled payloads with nonzero byte size, SHA-256, and package destinations; complete required-surface coverage; final-quality and rights review; release eligibility; source and license provenance; explicit credit or waiver lines; and an actual reviewed audio payload. It rejects raw/vendor paths, system fallbacks, placeholder/prototype/proof/temporary markers, silent-audio policy, incomplete credits, duplicate rows, and missing surface coverage. Its deterministic JSON and Markdown credits are invariant to input order. Focused strict-audit coverage passes 22 assertions in 3 cases; existing notices/BOM and release-license regressions pass 14 assertions in 2 cases and 12 assertions in 2 cases. The legacy bounded-starter gate still passes and writes build/reports/product_completion/pcq605_release_required_assets.json. The current release manifest is not final-quality evidence: it still explicitly permits prototype actors, proof/starter UI/VFX, silent audio, and system fallbacks, while CREDITS.md records unresolved redistribution/legal review. Selection and promotion of cohesive final actor/enemy/UI/audio/font payloads, runtime attachment, generated final credits, visual/audio review, legal signoff, clean-commit evidence, and release qualification remain pending.

FirstRunCalibrationFlow now provides a bounded, explicit journey across welcome, text scale, master audio preview, display and safe area, preferred input device, accessibility shortcuts, review, and completion. Fresh profiles run once; skipping persists safe defaults and remains replayable; completed profiles reject accidental first-run restarts; runtime settings expose a dedicated Replay Calibration route; cancelling a replay restores the baseline without writing. Text, audio, dimensions, and safe area are clamped before atomic persistence through the existing runtime settings authority. RuntimeSettings now round-trips safe-area scale, text scale, shortcut preference, calibration completion/skip/revision, and normalized auto/keyboard-mouse/controller preference while retaining the existing v1 schema compatibility. Focused calibration coverage passes 68 assertions in 4 cases; runtime settings, options route, and shell regressions pass 19 assertions in 1 case, 38 assertions in 3 cases, and 62 assertions in 3 cases. The source-matching urpg_tests target built successfully after serial recovery of the damaged Ninja log. Concrete startup/SceneManager presentation, rendered calibration surfaces, actual device discovery, audio playback and safe-area preview adapters, manual fresh-profile/controller proof, screenshots/video, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

VerticalSlicePacingReview now defines one bounded seven-category authority for time to control, menu depth, tutorial interruption, repeated confirmations, reward cadence, load masking, and blocking idle waits. Every observation requires a stable checkpoint and route; objective budgets classify friction; every breach requires an annotation; avoidable friction cannot pass without an implemented resolution; unavoidable friction requires explicit mitigation; and incomplete category coverage fails. Deterministic annotated-playthrough Markdown lists each route, measurement, finding, and resolution. The automated representative fixture covers all seven categories and proves that an over-budget first-reward cadence and blocking battle-result flourish pass only after concrete resolutions, while a minimum-hardware map transfer is admitted only with documented non-blocking transition masking. Focused pacing coverage passes 21 assertions in 3 cases; runtime shell and shared feedback regressions pass 62 assertions in 3 cases and 113 assertions in 4 cases. During validation, Ninja's stale dependency database was repaired with recompact plus one uninterrupted serial rebuild; dry-run and real incremental urpg_tests builds now report no work, the real check completes in 0.09 seconds, and the premature-EOF recovery warning is gone. Actual instrumented vertical-slice capture, reviewer-authored observations, implementation and recapture of every measured avoidable friction, target-hardware timing, screenshots/video, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

ProductBenchmarkSuite defines versioned tiny, medium, and large representative project fixtures plus minimum, recommended, and high-end desktop classes. A complete baseline requires all 81 fixture/hardware measurements across startup, project open, save, search, map edit, playtest launch, frame pacing, package, and memory, with explicit units, sample counts, and regression thresholds. Missing rows and threshold regressions fail visibly in deterministic JSON. The combined PCQ-700–707 and adjacent regression run passes 526 assertions in 45 cases. Actual generated fixture projects, benchmark executors, target-hardware captures, approved thresholds, versioned report files, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

PrimaryRouteWorkAudit covers project open, asset browse, search, map edit, save, playtest launch, package, and project graph. It rejects main-thread scans, blocking I/O, unbounded jobs, absent incremental indexes on scan-heavy routes, acknowledgement above 50 ms, and p95 latency beyond an authored budget. BoundedWorkQueue enforces FIFO work-unit slices and queue capacity; IncrementalRouteIndex applies stable-key updates and bounded deterministic search. The combined batch run passes 526 assertions in 45 cases. Concrete adoption by every primary route, instrumented interaction traces, approved budgets, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

StressScenarioSuite requires repeated open/close, playtest, package, large undo, asset churn, device churn, save cycles, and suspend/minimize runs. Each run has monotonic samples, minimum iterations, deterministic final-state hashes, bounded memory/handles/undo/jobs, responsive execution, and zero final pending jobs; corruption, deadlock, unresponsiveness, growth, and unrecovered jobs fail explicitly. The combined batch run passes 526 assertions in 45 cases. Process-level scenario drivers, long-duration real-project runs, target-hardware resource capture, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

FaultInjectionSuite provides explicit injection seams for disk full, permission loss, interrupted write, malformed document, missing asset, bad archive, failed migration, renderer/device loss, and child-process failure. Every handler must observe the fault, finish within a budget, preserve project data, contain partial state, emit an actionable diagnostic, and expose retry or recovery; missing, throwing, unsafe, or incomplete handlers fail. Existing project recovery and asset checkpoint regressions are included in the 526-assertion, 45-case combined pass. Concrete subsystem adapters and OS/device/process-level injections, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

SanitizerFuzzCoverage requires ASan, UBSan, TSan, and MSan lanes to be either enabled on a supporting toolchain or accompanied by an explicit blocker and alternative coverage. Bounded executable fuzz targets and corpus routing cover schemas, archives, event streams, and compatibility boundaries; oversized, missing, unrouted, unhandled, or throwing inputs fail. The combined batch run passes 526 assertions in 45 cases. Fresh Clang sanitizer builds, persistent fuzz corpora/runners, crash artifact retention, CI integration, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

ReleaseSecurityAudit produces a deterministic threat model across external processes, archive extraction, path containment, plugin/mod trust, secrets, network defaults, logs, and support bundles. Each surface requires a named owner/control, adversarial fixture, default-deny behavior, bounded execution, and secret-free output. Conservative relative-path and likely-secret helpers reject traversal, absolute/UNC paths, credentials, authorization headers, and private-key markers. The combined batch run passes 526 assertions in 45 cases. Static repository/process/archive audit integration, broader encoded-secret corpus, concrete adversarial package runs, reviewed threat model, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

PrivacyNetworkGate defines offline-first, no-automatic-upload defaults with mandatory reviewed endpoint IDs, user initiation, payload preview, explicit consent, telemetry opt-in, bounded retention, and deletion. Automatic telemetry, support, AI-provider, update, and multiplayer requests are denied; only previewed consented user actions enter the allowed ledger, which supports erasure and exposes unexpected-outbound counts. Existing analytics privacy and support-bundle regressions are included in the 526-assertion, 45-case combined pass. Wiring every network-capable owner through the gate, packet capture of a default session, retention/deletion persistence, privacy review, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

ReleaseSbomBuilder deterministically covers binaries, tools, packaged assets, optional providers, and research outputs in an SPDX-2.3-shaped document plus human notices. Every component requires stable identity, version, source, and license; included release payloads additionally require SHA-256 and redistribution approval. Missing classes, duplicate IDs, unresolved provenance/licenses, invalid hashes, and unapproved included content block release. Existing asset notices/BOM regressions are included in the 526-assertion, 45-case combined pass. Build/package dependency discovery, actual binary and tool hashes, transitive dependency enumeration, emitted package SBOM/notices, legal review, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

PlatformServicesProfile defines typed lifecycle, user, storage, input, display, achievement, presence, network, virtual-keyboard, locale, clock, suspend/power, and error capabilities with explicit available, unavailable, and degraded states. Headless and desktop fakes support deterministic auditing; missing runtime-required capabilities and direct desktop assumptions fail visibly. The combined PCQ-750–756 run passes 35 assertions in 10 cases. Concrete subsystem adoption, platform SDK adapters, hardware lifecycle testing, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

The platform-services boundary removes implicit desktop availability from runtime-required capability checks and provides deterministic unavailable/degraded behavior through headless and desktop fakes. The combined PCQ-750–756 run passes 35 assertions in 10 cases. Replacing remaining direct OS calls, device-loss and suspend/resume integration, target SDK certification, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

DesktopReleaseContract governs executable, runtime-library, content, license, and notice layout; safe relative paths and hashes; install, uninstall, portable saves, repair, and clean-smoke obligations; and agreement between UI, CLI, documentation, and readiness claims. The combined PCQ-750–756 run passes 35 assertions in 10 cases. Real installers, clean-machine smoke runs, upgrade/uninstall preservation proof, signing, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

VersionCompatibilityPolicy requires explicit supported ranges, rollback artifacts, downgrade messaging, N-1 coverage, and recovery proof for project schemas, saves, runtime, plugins/mods, packages, and updates. The combined PCQ-750–756 run passes 35 assertions in 10 cases. Wiring the policy into open/load/package/update routes, real N-1 artifacts, migration fixtures, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

Target support records now require UI, CLI, documentation, and readiness authorities to agree, while unsupported web and unavailable targets cannot be presented as qualified. The combined PCQ-750–756 run passes 35 assertions in 10 cases. Final target decisions, actual target packages and smoke evidence, public claim review, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

GovernedPackageManifest emits deterministic content hashes, references, licenses, notices, capability declarations, version metadata, and reproducibility diagnostics, including a structured explanation of differences. The combined PCQ-750–756 run passes 35 assertions in 10 cases. Integration with the real packager, byte-for-byte clean-build comparison, signed manifest emission, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

ReleaseProvenanceBuilder records channel, version, build, commit, compiler, target, runtime and package hashes, dirty state, and a support-facing version while rejecting secrets, workstation paths, invalid hashes, and dirty stable builds. The combined PCQ-750–756 run passes 35 assertions in 10 cases. Build-system population, package embedding, support UI exposure, clean-candidate provenance, and release signoff remain pending.

MenuAuthoringDocument extends the existing direct-manipulation preview and scene graph with a persistent hierarchy, multi-selection, constrained move/resize, snapping, alignment, distribution, safe area, zoom, responsive anchors, and bounded undo/redo. Its versioned JSON round trip retains geometry, routes, bindings, component instances, states, and transitions. Authoring documents now materialize panels/buttons into the native MenuSceneGraph and MenuPreviewPanel owns a safe preview graph for that runtime representation. The combined production-integration regression passes 1,073 assertions in 72 settings/menu/input cases. Full ImGui hierarchy/tool exposure, runtime pixel comparison at target viewports, migration corpus, manual screenshots, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

MenuComponentLibrary provides stable versioned definitions, slots, style tokens, visual variants, instance creation, impact previews, and controlled updates that preserve instance override keys and values. The combined menu run passes 335 assertions in 24 cases. Editor library browsing, find-uses integration, rendered component comparison, template upgrade UX, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

Menu nodes define default, focus, pressed, disabled, selected, loading, and error styles plus bounded entrance/exit-capable transitions, replacement/queue/blend interruption policy, reduced-motion collapse, and optional audio hooks. States and transitions round trip, and MenuPreviewPanel now resolves focused/disabled visual properties, transition duration, audio hooks, audio-off behavior, and reduced-motion collapse from the authored document. The integration regression passes 628 assertions in 67 menu/accessibility cases. Concrete renderer/audio playback consumption, keyboard/controller/touch-like simulation across every component, visual capture, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

Typed menu bindings resolve project, runtime, save, and localization sources as string, integer, number, or boolean values with declared fallbacks and formatting. Menu runtime materialization now consumes label, enabled, and visibility bindings from preview fixtures; missing required data renders the authored fallback and emits explicit diagnostics instead of silently packaging. The integration regression passes 628 assertions in 67 menu/accessibility cases. Binding-picker UI, live project/save adapter population, plural/date/number formatters, locale fixture corpus, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

Menu authoring audit resolves target canvases and reports overflow, required actions outside safe areas, missing labels, broken focus edges, unreachable focus nodes, and text expansion overflow. It exposes five target-resolution presets and keyboard/mouse, generic-controller, and touch-like glyph-preview modes. MenuPreviewPanel now carries authored state and reduced-motion/audio policy into its inspectable runtime snapshot. The integration regression passes 628 assertions in 67 menu/accessibility cases. Editor overlays, platform-specific glyph packs, automated screenshot matrix, manual controller review, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

MenuStarterTemplateLibrary ships original editable URPG authoring documents for title, save/load, settings, pause, inventory, equipment, quest log, dialogue, shop, battle HUD, and results. Every starter has safe-area-contained required actions, a complete focus cycle, accessible labels, deterministic document round trip, and a stable custom route that materializes into the native runtime graph and preview panel. The combined production-integration regression passes 1,073 assertions in 72 settings/menu/input cases. First-party visual art/content refinement, concrete application-route handlers, package fixtures, accessibility and visual review, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

UnifiedInputRouter governs hot-plug state, optional player ownership, contexts, alternative controls and chords, axes, deadzones, repeat cadence, conflicts, calibration, active-device glyphs, and recovery. ControllerInputProvider aggregates multi-device sources safely into InputCore, preventing one disconnect from releasing an action still held elsewhere. SDLSurface enumerates and hot-plugs controllers, maps D-pad/face/shoulder buttons and left-stick axes, selects Xbox/PlayStation/Switch glyph families, and releases held actions on disconnect. Runtime settings persist a dedicated controller-binding path; ControllerBindingRuntime atomically saves/loads it with malformed-file rollback, and runtime startup applies complete mappings before SDL initialization. The editor now exposes controller assignments through the governed Map-authoring route, swaps conflicting actions without losing required coverage, reports invalid bindings, restores defaults as an undoable dirty-state boundary, applies valid changes live through SDL, saves to config/controller_bindings.json, and includes the document in private recovery snapshots. Keyboard mappings now save to the runtime's canonical config/input_mappings.json path while retaining legacy input_remap.json loading. The MinGW SDL 2.30 compatibility guard restores Joystick, Haptic, HIDAPI Joystick, Virtual Joystick, and XInput in the actual build; runtime, editor, and tests link against it, and a virtual-controller fixture proves enumerate/map/open/button-event behavior. The grouped regression passes 126 assertions in 11 cases and Ninja reports no remaining work after linking urpg_tests, urpg_editor, and urpg_runtime. Physical multi-controller hardware testing, controller-only journey capture, manual editor remap review, clean-commit evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

Runtime Options exposes all declared settings in a controller/keyboard-navigable bounded viewport with live preview, persisted Save, cancel rollback, and safe reset. InclusiveRuntimePolicy derives one validated design/feedback/render policy and applies it to the runtime shell, exploration, battle, and renderer consumers. Runtime startup, live Options preview, Save, and cancel rollback now update deterministic color matrices in both immediate and textured OpenGL shaders. Battle overlay-emphasis cues produce short fading screen flashes whose opacity is capped by the inclusive flash setting, including a zero-flash mode. Voice is a first-class AudioCategory rather than sharing effects, survives mix-preset serialization, is visible in editor diagnostics/mix UI, is applied as voice times master volume at runtime startup, and authored dialogue routes through it. The PCQ-651 slice passes 105 assertions in 8 cases, runtime-policy coverage passes 45 assertions in 4 cases, visual-regression/OpenGL coverage passes 104 assertions in 14 cases, and the focused startup voice-volume integration passes 8 assertions in 1 case. Implementation closure is complete; manual visual/audio accessibility review, clean-candidate evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

entries.notes: The canonical localization bundle schema and LocaleCatalog own legacy strings plus structured zero/one/two/few/many/other plural forms and neutral/masculine/feminine/other grammar variants. The same authority carries fallback locale, text direction, governed font profile, IME support, and source revision through runtime import, document writeback, editor preview, and the consistency gate. InclusiveLocalizationModel resolves major plural families, localized digits, grouped decimals, and regional dates. A permanent English, RTL Arabic, and expanded en-XA corpus passes the consistency gate. The renderer boundary carries locale, font-profile ID, and direction metadata into deterministic UTF-8, combining-cluster, CJK-wrap, mixed RTL/numeric, punctuation-mirroring, and contextual-Arabic layout. Project-scoped urpg.font_profiles.v1 manifests now resolve ordered TrueType fallback faces only within project content, reject unsafe or invalid faces, audit required sample strings and locale-profile references, and expose issues in the editor. Runtime and editor startup share that exact registry with OpenGL, which caches linearly filtered Unicode text textures, reports missing glyphs once, and refuses unresolved profile fallback in release mode. Permanent good and known-bad font-profile fixtures cover Latin, Arabic, CJK, path traversal, invalid faces, impossible glyphs, raster output, and audit integration without promoting the test fonts as licensed release assets. This checkpoint passes 28 font-profile assertions in 2 cases, 99 PCQ-652 assertions in 7 cases, 62 catalog assertions in 11 cases, 52 runtime-dialogue assertions in 4 cases, and 10 focused EngineShell startup assertions. Full standards-conformant complex-script shaping still requires a governed dependency decision; shipping font licensing/promotion, RTL/IME manual capture, clean-candidate evidence, and release signoff remain pending.

Caption-track validation requires stable cues, speaker identity, localized text, locale/take identity, attached muted alternatives, increasing timing, voice alignment within 250 ms, required locale coverage, and non-empty structured non-speech cues. DialogueGraph now persists ordered locale voice takes, take IDs, asset IDs, measured durations, muted-alternative asset IDs, caption timing, caption localization keys, and non-speech cues while preserving legacy single-voice documents.
